hook: After the *Buzzer*, the Knicks Walk Into a Trap
dek: Knicks host Pacers tonight at MSG, a night after Mikal Bridges' buzzer-beater 3.

slides.label: Tonight's Game
slides.text: Pacers at Knicks, Sunday, Nov. 22, *8 p.m. ET* at Madison Square Garden. Watch on MSG Network or DAZN.

slides.label: Saturday's Chaos
slides.text: The Knicks led by *26* over Portland, then watched it all vanish as the Blazers stormed back in the third quarter.

slides.label: The Shot
slides.text: Down 96-94 with 3.4 seconds left, Josh Hart found Mikal Bridges, who buried his second 3 of the night at the horn.

slides.label: Trap Game
slides.text: The Knicks are banged up on a back to back, but the Pacers are missing *Tyrese Haliburton* and more.

slides.label: Revenge Spot
slides.text: Indiana already beat New York 106-104 on Nov. 13, an *NBA Cup* loss that still stings for the champs.

slides.label: Cup Math
slides.text: New York is *0-2* in Cup group play. They must win Wednesday vs. Cleveland and Friday vs. Miami, then get help.

slides.label: Homestand
slides.text: Four straight games at the Garden: Pacers, Cavaliers, Heat (Prime Video, Black Friday) and Hawks.

slides.label: Bottom Line
slides.text: Tonight protects the streak. Wednesday and Friday decide if the *defending champs* have any Cup run left.

caption_instagram:
Knicks vs Pacers tonight at Madison Square Garden isn't just a Sunday game, it's a trap game dressed up as a victory lap. One night after Mikal Bridges buried a buzzer beating 3 to beat Portland 97-96, Jalen Brunson and the defending champs are back at the Garden on a back to back, banged up and four games deep into a brutal stretch.

The good news: Indiana is worse off, missing Tyrese Haliburton and more. The bad news: the Pacers already beat New York once this season, in an NBA Cup game that still stings. Tonight doesn't count toward the Cup, but Wednesday against Cleveland and Friday against Miami do, and the Knicks are 0-2 in group play with no room left for slip ups.

Four straight games at the Garden this week. One banner hanging. Zero guarantees.

caption_linkedin:
The Knicks' last 24 hours are a case study for anyone building something. Saturday night they built a 26 point lead, watched it evaporate against Portland, then still found a way to win on a Mikal Bridges buzzer beater. That is not luck. That is a team that trusts its habits when the plan falls apart.

Tonight they host the Pacers at Madison Square Garden on a back to back, short handed, defending a four game win streak. The real test isn't tonight though, it's Wednesday and Friday, when NBA Cup games against Cleveland and Miami decide whether the defending champions still have a path forward. New York is already 0-2 in group play. No margin left.

Founders know this rhythm. The win that gets the headlines rarely tells you the whole story. It's the unglamorous back to back, the short bench, the game that does not even count on paper, that tells you who you really are.
